_about: Food items fish eat, with when and where each is active. Hand-built starter hatch chart; months are 1-12. 'peak' = main hatch or feeding window, 'on' = present but not peak. Season keys are regions or 'all': an empty entry keeps a food out of season all year there, a food with no northeast entry uses its east one, and one with no south entry uses the east's shifted a month earlier when it has no 'all' (rules._season_spec). Water keys may be a water type or a group (RIVER, LAKE, WARM, SALT). Sizes are hook numbers [largest, smallest]; 0 = 1/0, -1 = 2/0, -2 = 3/0.

foods.name: Midges
foods.desc: Tiny midge larvae, pupae and adults; the year-round staple, key in winter and on tailwaters

foods.name: Chironomids
foods.desc: Lake midge pupae rising from the bottom; the main lake food in spring and fall

foods.name: Blue-winged olives
foods.desc: Small olive mayflies (Baetis); hatch best on cool overcast or drizzly afternoons in spring and fall

foods.name: Pale morning duns
foods.desc: Yellow-olive western mayflies that hatch late morning through summer

foods.name: Hendricksons
foods.desc: Classic eastern early-season mayfly hatching in mid-afternoon

foods.name: Sulfurs
foods.desc: Pale yellow eastern mayflies hatching at dusk in late spring

foods.name: March browns
foods.desc: Large mottled mayflies; spring in the West, late spring in the East

foods.name: Green drakes
foods.desc: Big green mayflies with a short, intense early-summer hatch

foods.name: Tricos
foods.desc: Tiny black-and-white mayflies; morning spinner falls on summer spring creeks and tailwaters

foods.name: Callibaetis
foods.desc: Speckled lake mayflies that hatch midday in summer

foods.name: Caddisflies
foods.desc: Tent-winged caddis; pupae and skittering adults, strongest in the evening from spring to fall

foods.name: October caddis
foods.desc: Big orange fall caddis on western freestone rivers

foods.name: Salmonflies
foods.desc: Huge orange stoneflies; the famous western freestone hatch of early summer

foods.name: Golden stoneflies
foods.desc: Large golden stoneflies that follow or overlap the salmonflies

foods.name: Yellow sallies
foods.desc: Small yellow stoneflies laying eggs in the evening

foods.name: Stonefly nymphs
foods.desc: Big stonefly nymphs living in fast rocky water all year; heavy mouthfuls bounced along the bottom

foods.name: Grasshoppers
foods.desc: Grasshoppers blown into the water along grassy banks on hot, windy summer afternoons

foods.name: Ants
foods.desc: Ants falling in all summer; trout rarely refuse them

foods.name: Beetles
foods.desc: Beetles dropping from bankside trees and grass in summer

foods.name: Scuds
foods.desc: Freshwater shrimp in weedy tailwaters, spring creeks and lakes all year

foods.name: Sowbugs
foods.desc: Aquatic sowbugs; a year-round staple on weedy tailwaters and spring creeks

foods.name: Aquatic worms
foods.desc: Worms washed into the river; best during high or rising dirty water

foods.name: Fish eggs
foods.desc: Drifting eggs during trout and salmon spawning runs, and sucker eggs in spring

foods.name: Leeches
foods.desc: Undulating leeches in lakes and slower rivers; good all year, great in low light

foods.name: Sculpins
foods.desc: Bottom-hugging baitfish that big trout hunt, especially in cold, high or off-color water

foods.name: Minnows and fry
foods.desc: Small trout-water minnows, dace, and spring fry

foods.name: Crayfish
foods.desc: Crayfish scuttling over rocks in warmer months; a bass favorite

foods.name: Damselflies
foods.desc: Slim olive damsel nymphs swimming toward shore in early summer lakes

foods.name: Dragonfly nymphs
foods.desc: Chunky dragonfly nymphs crawling in lake weed beds

foods.name: Crane flies
foods.desc: Fat crane fly larvae washed out of banks, and gangly fall adults

foods.name: Mice
foods.desc: Mice swimming across at night; big trout and bass eat them in summer

foods.name: Frogs
foods.desc: Frogs along lily pads and grassy edges of warm ponds

foods.name: Surface bugs
foods.desc: Big insects, cicadas and struggling bugs on warm water; bass and panfish pop them off the top

foods.name: Shad and shiners
foods.desc: Shad, shiners and small sunfish; the main forage for bass

foods.name: Hellgrammites
foods.desc: Dobsonfly larvae under rocks in warmwater rivers; smallmouth candy

foods.name: Shrimp
foods.desc: Grass and snapping shrimp on warm flats; the core bonefish and redfish food

foods.name: Crabs
foods.desc: Small crabs on flats and marsh edges; permit and redfish key on them

foods.name: Sand eels
foods.desc: Slim sand eels in the surf; big fuel for spring and fall striper runs

foods.name: Saltwater baitfish
foods.desc: Menhaden, mullet, silversides and anchovies moving along beaches and estuaries

foods.name: Squid
foods.desc: Squid pushing into spring striper water

foods.name: Cinder worm hatch
foods.desc: Spawning worms swarming estuaries on warm late-spring evenings

foods.name: Isonychia (slate drakes)
foods.desc: Big dark swimming mayflies of eastern and southern freestones; nymphs crawl out on rocks, duns and spinners come off in the evening in early summer and again in fall

foods.name: Smelt
foods.desc: Rainbow smelt, the main food of landlocked salmon and big brook trout in northern New England lakes and the rivers that drain them; they run upstream to spawn after ice-out and school again in fall
